messages:
sara: saw a ~12% p95 latency regression on ingress over the last deploy. root cause looks host-side not model decode. filing here before digging deeper. p50 unchanged, p95 from 210ms -> 235ms, CPU on ingress proxy up +18%. :eyes:
kevin: ugh. any quick trace IDs or flamegraphs? do we have a before/after diff from the deploy?
nora: grabbed a quick perf profile from the canary (trace id t-9f3b). flamegraph shows an uptick in tokenization and grpc write path. attaching snippet: `grpc->serialize_headers` and `tokenize::normalize` both heavier.
alex: did we change kernel selection heuristics or batching recently? those can shift KV cache locality and cause extra host parsing.
sara: we rolled the compile patch that added micro-kernel for mixed-quant convs two days ago. I thought that only touched device runtime but maybe endpoint routing changed. also turned on proto-fragment coalescing in sidecar.
kevin: can you paste the profile command you used? I want the raw perf map.
nora: ran `perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 30` on the ingress host then `perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl | flamegraph.pl > flame.svg`. sharing quick ASCII snapshot of top stacks:
```
  18.2% tokenize::normalize
  12.5% grpc::writev
  8.7% ingress::parse_frame
  6.1% kvcache::lookup
  5.8% http2::framer
```
sara: interesting kvcache lookup looks smaller than expected but addtl CPU in tokenize + grpc. i also noticed more small writes on the socket. looks like streaming chunking now emits more micro-fragments.
alex: small writes -> Nagle disabled? or grpc writev fragmentation. Which client path? http/1.1 gateway or grpc ingress?
sara: both. we have HTTP clients hitting the gateway which proxies to gRPC. gateway had proto-fragment coalescer toggled to `fast-path` last week. may be creating more, smaller proto blobs to the sidecar.
kevin: hypothesis: compile/kernel change changed batching heuristics (recompute of suggested batch size) so requests are getting split into smaller micro-batches -> more tokenization calls + more small gRPC writes.
nora: i probed kv cache hit-rate for the canary vs baseline: baseline hit 74%, canary 59% over same workload. that explains more kv lookups failing and falling back to CPU-heavy tokenization.
sara: nice find. do we have decision log where kernel patch touched batching heuristic recompute?
alex: yes the kernel selection PR included a heuristic: if sequence_length_stddev < 6 then prefer kernel-A which uses smaller per-request batching window. will paste PR link.
perf-bot: benchmark results uploaded: https://artifacts.internal/redwood/perf/3850012345/compare.html (before vs after). summary: ingress CPU +16%, p95 latency +12%.
kevin: next steps: 1) bisect kernel PR -> confirm causality 2) revert proto-fragment fast-path in gateway 3) add temporary batching cap to prevent micro-batches 4) re-run kvcache warmup experiment. anyone wants to take ownership?
sara: i'll bisect the kernel PR and run the canary with kernel pinned to previous. estimated 2-3 hours.
nora: i'll disable fast-path in gateway and run kv warmup experiment after sara's bisect completes.
alex: i'll prepare a quick patch that enforces a min-batch-size (config flag `min_batch_tokens=64`) we can flip remotely. small code sample for heuristic guard:
```
if (suggested_batch_tokens < cfg.min_batch_tokens) {
  suggested_batch_tokens = cfg.min_batch_tokens;
}
```
kevin: add telemetry for writev call sizes to confirm fragmentation drop. also log KV cache miss source to see whether misses are from variant selection or eviction.
sara: noted. I'll post back with bisect results here. thanks all. :thumbsup:
